question: Should it be a crime not to help a stranger in danger when helping carries no risk?
answer: France punishes a bystander who could safely help, or call for help, and does neither: up to five years in prison and a €75,000 fine. The law asks only what any decent person would do anyway, and a floor matters most on the day when everyone present assumes someone else will act.
move: Whichever side you took, the question is whether a law can draw the line.
counterpoint: Thomas Macaulay, drafting India's penal code in 1837, asked where such a law stops: is the rich man who lets a beggar starve a criminal, or the only surgeon able to operate who will not make the journey? Law can forbid harm cleanly. Commanding help makes every bystander a suspect, and punishes the frightened along with the callous.
reference: Code pénal (France), article 223-6, in force since 1994; Macaulay, Notes on the Indian Penal Code, Note M, 1837
